# dev fails its own size guard, so every open PR is asked to fix a baseline it never touched

## Context

Surfaced by @tobiu at 2026-09-04 ~22:45Z on the rebased Dependabot PR #18325, whose File Size Guard job reads:

```
FAIL over-target  1419 code |  1785 doc (49.2%)  src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs

check-file-sizes: 1 violation(s).
  src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs: lower the HEAD baseline from 1740 to the measured count 1419.
```

His read, and it is the right one: *"that makes no sense for dependabot."* A bot bumping npm versions cannot lower a code-line baseline, and it has no business being asked to.

Reproduced on `dev@b7c9f7c953` itself, with no PR involved:

```
$ npm run check-file-sizes
FAIL over-target  1419 code |  1785 doc (49.2%)  src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs
check-file-sizes: 1 violation(s).
  src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs: HEAD baseline must equal the measured count 1419.
```

**`dev` fails its own guard.** Live latest-open sweep: checked the latest 20 open issues at 2026-09-04T22:47:04Z; the only file-size ticket is #18278, closed. A2A claim sweep over the current mailbox window: no claim on this scope. Own-assignment sweep: none on the build surface.

## The Problem

Merge order, and nothing else.

| commit | time | what it did |
|---|---|---|
| `0cc5cad95e` (#18305 / PR #18324) | 22:15Z | maximize became a plugin — `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs` **1740 → 1419 code lines** |
| `33d12ba837` (#18278 / PR #18333) | 22:22Z | the size guard merged, carrying `file-size-baseline.json` with **1740** |

The guard's baseline was measured before the shrink landed and merged after it, so `dev` shipped a baseline that disagrees with `dev`'s own tree by 321 lines.

Every PR then inherits the stale `1740` as **both** its base and HEAD baseline, measures `1419`, and takes the shrink branch of the ratchet — which correctly requires the HEAD entry to be lowered in the same change. The requirement is right; the PR being asked is arbitrary. Dependabot cannot satisfy it, and neither should anyone else whose diff never touched that file.

**The ratchet is not the defect, and this ticket must not be read as a case against it.** Once `dev` reads `1419`, an untouched file gives `base == head == measured`, the equality branch passes, and nothing is asked of any PR. Going forward the invariant is self-maintaining: a PR that shrinks a baselined file is required to lower the row in the same commit, so `dev` cannot drift again through the normal path. What happened here is a one-time artifact of the guard's own introduction racing a shrink that predated it.

**This is my miss.** I approved #18333 at 22:17Z — two minutes after #18324 had already merged. I verified the baseline file's contents and the four counts as the author reported them, and never re-measured them against the tree they would land on. A baseline is a witness minted at authoring time; between authoring and merge, the thing it witnesses can move.

## The Architectural Reality

- `buildScripts/util/check-file-sizes.mjs` — `evaluateMeasurements`, the `current < baseValue` branch: `if (headValue !== current) fail('lower the HEAD baseline …')`. Correct as written; it is answering a question about a tree whose baseline row is stale.
- `buildScripts/util/file-size-baseline.json` — `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs: 1740`, against a measured `1419` at `dev@b7c9f7c953`. The other three rows are current: Workstation `3390`, DemoB `2701`, DragDrop `1267`.
- `.github/workflows/file-size-guard.yml` runs only on `pull_request`, so `dev` never audits itself and the inconsistency is invisible until it fails somebody else's PR.
- `--fix` already produces exactly the required edit (`reconcileBaseline` writes measured over-target counts), so no new capability is needed.

## The Fix

Lower `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs` to `1419` in `buildScripts/util/file-size-baseline.json`, generated with `npm run check-file-sizes -- --fix` rather than typed.

That is the whole change. It unblocks every open PR at once, because the stale row was the only violation.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `file-size-baseline.json` | #18278's ratchet — a shrink lowers the entry | `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs: 1740 → 1419`; the other three rows unchanged | none needed — `--fix` is idempotent and regenerates from measurement | `learn/guides/advanced/BuildArchitecture.md` §7 already documents `--fix` | `npm run check-file-sizes` exits 0 on `dev` after the change, and the four rows still report |

## Decision Record impact

`none` — a stale generated value, not a contract change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 — `npm run check-file-sizes` on this branch reports 0 violations and still lists all four baselined files with their bands.
- [ ] AC-2 — **Red-first, and it needs no construction:** `dev@b7c9f7c953` fails the same command with exactly one violation naming `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs`. The pre-state is the falsifier; record it rather than building a fixture.
- [ ] AC-3 — The baseline row equals the measured count `1419`, and was produced by `--fix`, not hand-edited. The other three rows are byte-identical to their current values — a `--fix` run that silently re-writes an unrelated row would mean the tree moved under a second file, which is a different finding and must not ride along unnoticed.
- [ ] AC-4 — The File Size Guard job passes on this PR, which is the first PR to exercise the guard against a consistent baseline.
- [ ] AC-5 — **Non-vacuity:** confirm the guard still fails on genuine growth after the fix. Raising the row by hand to `1420` (measured `1419`) must fail with the shrink message; restoring it must pass. A baseline correction that quietly disarmed the ratchet would satisfy AC-1 through AC-4.

## Out of Scope

- **Changing the ratchet so untouched files are exempt.** My first read, and it is wrong: with a consistent `dev` an untouched file hits the equality branch and passes, so the exemption would buy nothing and would remove the arm that catches a shrink whose PR forgot to lower the row.
- **A `dev`-side run of the guard.** Tempting — `dev` failing its own gate for seven minutes with nothing to notice it is the real gap here — but it is a workflow-surface change with its own required-check consequences, and this ticket is the unblock. Worth its own ticket if it recurs.
- Splitting `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs`. That is Epic #18304's work; this only records what #18324 already removed.

## Avoided Traps

- **Reading this as "the ratchet is broken."** The operator's framing was that the demand makes no sense for Dependabot, which is true of *this* PR and would have been true of any PR open at that moment. The mechanism is a stale row, not a bad rule, and fixing the rule would have been a redesign in response to a one-line defect.
- **Hand-editing the JSON.** The file is generated; typing `1419` would produce the right bytes today and detach the file from its generator. `--fix` is the documented path.
- **Treating the guard's own CI as the falsifier.** The guard runs only on `pull_request`, so a green `dev` says nothing about this. The reproduction has to be a local run against `dev`, which is what AC-2 records.
